notes: §1989:A.2.40.4 RV1: "The returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1." An 85 program has only native arithmetic (the OPTIONS paragraph's ARITHMETIC clause is refused at 85), so RenderDec's standard-decimal SqrtDec arm is not taken and FloatBody calls CobolIntrinsics.Sqrt: Math.Abs(Math.Sqrt(x)), the correctly rounded binary64 root made absolute (a negative zero returns +0), with a scaled operand past binary64's range rooted on the exact carrier first; RenderFloatNative lands it at the receiver's scale. Probed at --std 85: an 18-digit perfect square from an item and from a literal returns its exact root, and DISPLAY, COMP, COMP-3, signed-zero, nested and relation uses return the non-negative root. The witness takes the roots of 0, 1, 16, 2.25, 0.0625, 2 and an expression and tests the sign.

next.reason: 1989: 'The returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1', unconditionally. 2023 keeps those words only 'When native arithmetic is in effect' (§2023:15.84.4 RV4), the default when no ARITHMETIC clause is written (§2023:11.9.5.2 GR4), and adds cases: 'When standard-decimal arithmetic is in effect, the returned value is the absolute value of the exact square root of argument-1 rounded to 34 digits' (§2023:15.84.4 RV2) and the standard-binary case 'rounded to 113 significant bits' (§2023:15.84.4 RV3). A program selecting ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL or STANDARD-BINARY is accepted by 2023, not by 1985, and gets a different SQRT result: a case added, so CHANGED. RV2/RV3 state the added cases, not the 1989 requirement, so 'to' names RV4.
